claims.claim: The Brain authoring contract requires newly authored acceptance criteria to describe pre-verification implementation properties claimable by any admitted Executor and assigns later lifecycle facts to their existing authorities.

All three adapters instruct PRIMARY and REPAIR Executors to make affirmative implementation claims, leave unconfirmable acceptance IDs uncovered, and reserve unresolved for concrete Executor-owned work or a material supplied-contract conflict.

The generic schema retains empty claims and non-empty unresolved capability with clarified descriptions. The dedicated finalization schema has a strict ResultPackage envelope, permits complete and incomplete payloads, and requires empty evidence arrays.

Each adapter selects the dedicated schema only for an exact bound FINALIZE_CANDIDATE action. MiniMax now describes all four REPAIR actions and the finalization candidate’s unchanged-head, zero-mutation, bounded-inspection semantics.
The implementation changes no Runtime completion gate or verification and EVIDENCE path; the finalization schema preserves unresolved and uncovered acceptance for those existing gates.
